titulo: I am thinking about my brother
intro: Each verb asks for its preposition. They are learned together: «pensar en», «soñar con», «depender de».
p.pensar en.consejo: To have someone in mind you use «en»: «pienso en ti». To give an opinion you use «de».
p.soñar con.consejo: It always takes «con»: «sueño con el mar». It is irregular: «sueño», «sueñas».
p.depender de.consejo: «De» and «el» merge: «depende del precio». You never say «depende en».
p.enamorarse de.consejo: You fall in love «de» someone. The stress is on «RAR»: e-na-mo-RAR-se.
p.acordarse de.consejo: It takes «de»: «me acuerdo de ti», «me acuerdo de que…». It is irregular: «me acuerdo».
p.darse cuenta de.consejo: With «que» you keep «de»: «me di cuenta de que…». Saying «me di cuenta que» is a common mistake.
p.casarse con.consejo: You marry «con» someone: «se casó con ella». You do not say «casarse a».
p.confiar en.consejo: It takes «en»: «confío en ti». The form «confío» has an accent on the i.
p.contar con.consejo: «Contar con» someone means being able to rely on their help: «cuenta conmigo».
p.tratar de.consejo: With an infinitive: «trato de dormir». It can also mean «to be about»: «trata de amor».
p.empezar a.consejo: With an infinitive it takes «a»: «empieza a llover». The e becomes ie: «empiezo».
p.acostumbrarse a.consejo: It takes «a»: «me acostumbro al frío». A noun or an infinitive can follow.
b1.texto:
Each verb asks for its own **preposition**. They are learned together.

- **Pensar en** someone: pienso **en** mi hermano. **Pensar de** something asks for an opinion: ¿qué piensas **de** la película?
- **Soñar con**, **casarse con**, **contar con**.
- **Depender de**, **enamorarse de**, **acordarse de**.

The preposition stays before **que**: me acuerdo **de que**…, me di cuenta **de que**…

In questions it goes before the question word: ¿**En qué** piensas? ¿**Con quién** se casó?
b2.f1.texto: I am thinking about my brother, who has fallen in love with a girl from Lima.
b2.f2.texto: And is he going to marry her?
b2.f5.texto: He trusts he will soon find a good position.
b2.f6.texto: Do you remember my cousin from Lima?
b2.f7.texto: Your brother can count on her.
b4.texto:
- with **en**: pensar en, confiar en, insistir en, fijarse en
- with **de**: depender de, enamorarse de, acordarse de, darse cuenta de, tratar de
- with **con**: soñar con, casarse con, contar con, encontrarse con
- with **a**: aprender a, empezar a, acostumbrarse a, atreverse a

Before **que** the preposition is kept: me acuerdo **de que** vienes.

In a question the preposition comes first: ¿**De qué** depende? ¿**Con quién** sueñas?
b4.e0.texto: I always think about my family.
b4.e1.texto: Who are you dreaming of tonight?
b4.e2.texto: I realised that a chair was missing.
b5.f0.texto: Every afternoon, Andrés sits by the window and thinks about the sea of Lima.
b5.f1.texto: He dreams of a long street, of wooden balconies and of the smell of warm bread.
b5.f2.texto: The mist from the harbour clings to the windowpanes like a white sigh.
b5.f3.texto: He is not yet used to the long winters or to the afternoons without sun.
b5.f4.texto: That is why he writes long letters and fills them with small promises.
b5.f5.texto: On the other side of the ocean, a young woman reads those letters with trembling hands.
b5.f6.texto: She trusts every word and falls in love little by little with the slanted handwriting.
b5.f7.texto: She notices the small details, an ink stain, a smell of the sea.
b5.f8.texto: Some day the two of them will meet under the same grey sky.
b5.f9.texto: In the meantime, she counts on patience and on the promises he writes.
b6.o0.refuerzo: Yes! «Pensar en» someone is to have them on your mind.
b6.o1.refuerzo: «Pensar de» asks for an opinion: «¿qué piensas de él?».
b6.o2.refuerzo: «Pensar» is not used with «a» in this sense.
b6.pregunta: You have someone on your mind. Which preposition?
b7.o0.refuerzo: With «de» you do not use «en qué»: the question gets mixed up.
b7.o1.refuerzo: That is it! «Pensar de» is used to ask for an opinion.
b7.o2.refuerzo: «Pensar en» does not ask for an opinion but for what is on your mind.
b7.pregunta: How do you ask for an opinion about the film?
b8.frase: No me había dado cuenta de nada
b9.o0.refuerzo: You do not say «depender en»: the verb asks for «de».
b10.o1.refuerzo: The preposition is missing in front: «¿con quién…?».
b10.pregunta: How do you ask «Who did she marry?»
b11.pregunta: Write in Spanish: «I dream of travelling».
b12.o0.refuerzo: «Acordarse» does not ask for «en» but for «de».
b12.o1.refuerzo: That is it! «Acordarse de» keeps «de» before «que».
p.piensas.consejo: Present of «pensar», for «tú». «¿Qué piensas?» asks for your opinion.
p.casar.consejo: Here «casar», with «se», means to marry. Infinitive used in «se va a casar».
p.confía.consejo: Present of «confiar», for «él» or «ella». Stress on «FI».
p.encontrar.consejo: Infinitive of «encontrar». It follows «confía en», so trust in finding.
p.acuerdas.consejo: Present of «acordarse», for «tú». It means you remember.
p.sueñas.consejo: From «soñar», to dream. The «ñ» sounds like «ny».
p.faltaba.consejo: Imperfect of «faltar». «Me di cuenta de que faltaba» means I noticed something was missing.
p.pega.consejo: From «pegar», to stick. The «g» before «a» sounds hard.
p.acostumbra.consejo: From «acostumbrarse», to get used to. «No se acostumbra» means he is not used to it yet.
p.temblorosas.consejo: Feminine plural, agreeing with «manos». Stress on «RO».
p.enamora.consejo: From «enamorarse», to fall in love. The «r» between vowels is soft.
p.inclinada.consejo: Feminine of «inclinado», agreeing with «letra». Stress on «NA».
p.fija.consejo: From «fijarse», to pay attention. The «j» sounds like «h».
p.detalles.consejo: Plural of «detalle», a small part. The «ll» sounds like «y».
p.encontrarán.consejo: Future of «encontrarse», for «ellos». The accent on the last «á» marks stress.
p.casó.consejo: Past tense of «casarse», for one person. The accent on «ó» shows stress.
